newsitem.title: USA: Lear acquisitions, sales mix boost Q1 net.
newsitem.headline: Lear acquisitions, sales mix boost Q1 net.

text.p: Lear Corp said Tuesday that acquisitions and favorable mix of automotive interior components sales helped it to post record earnings for the first quarter of fiscal 1997.
Lear said its net income for the quarter ended March 29 rose 62.4 percent to $41.9 million, or $0.62 a share, from year-earlier earnings of $25.8 million, or $0.43 a share.

"Our strategic acquisition program, in tandem with internally generated sales and a favorable program mix, remain the primary drivers for Lear's sales and earnings growth," Lear Chairman Kenneth Way said in a statement.
Net sales for the first quarter of 1997 were $1.7 billion, compared to $1.4 billion in the first quarter of 1996.

The $318.2 million first quarter sales increase is attributable to internal growth as well as additional revenues from the acquisitions of Masland and Borealis acquisitions, which contributed $159.9 million and $47.7 million, respectively.
Geographically, 23 percent of the first quarter's sales increase was attributable to Lear's operations outside of the U.S. and Canada.

Sales for Lear's European operations rose 8 percent to $415.1 million, while sales in Mexico and other world regions advanced 39 percent to $147.3 million. First quarter sales in the United States and Canada increased more than 26 percent to approximately $1.2 billion.

Way said he is confident that the company's focus on service, global one-stop shopping and high quality, low-cost products "will enable us to expand our global growth and achieve excellent financial performance for our shareholders."
